title: Alignment runbook for mid-cycle tradeoffs and rolling capacity landing zone
creator: Jordan Park
description: Problem: mid-cycle we see significant scope churn as urgent customer requests, incidents, and high-visibility growth experiments collide with committed roadmap work. This leads to brittle tradeoffs, uncoordinated scope cuts, and morale-impacting last-minute reallocations. Goal: provide a lightweight, repeatable runbook ("Landing Zone") that product, eng, and design can use to make transparent, data-driven tradeoffs that preserve predictability for high-cost roadmap items while reserving capacity for emergent needs.
overview: This ticket captures a runbook and a set of rules: 1) a rolling capacity grid with named lanes, 2) a fast feature scoring rubric to prioritize mid-cycle requests, 3) escalation and rollback triggers, and 4) a comms template for announcing cuts and swaps to stakeholders.
landing_zone_definition:
Landing Zone lanes (default allocations):
- Core Roadmap: 60% of cycle team capacity (blocked by 'commit' flag).
- Maintenance & Reliability: 15% (SLO work, tech debt with agreed acceptance criteria).
- Customer/Emergent: 15% (high-touch accounts, paid remediation).
- Experiments/Growth: 10% (timeboxed A/B tests, product discovery).
Lanes are soft for small teams but provide guardrails. Each lane must publish 1-line entry describing the highest priority item and owner at start of cycle.
scoring_rubric: Use 4 dimensions, each scored 1-5: Impact (customer value / revenue), Effort (dev+design+qa), Risk (security/regulatory/deploy risk), Dependency Complexity. Weighted score = 0.4*Impact - 0.2*Effort - 0.2*Risk - 0.2*DependencyComplexity. Normalize to -5..+5. Decision rules: >=2.5 -> promote to Core Roadmap candidate, 1.0-2.5 -> consider as fill-in (Customer/Emergent or Experiments), <1 -> defer. Example: Feature X: Impact 5, Effort 3, Risk 2, Dep 2 -> Score = 0.4*5 - 0.2*3 - 0.2*2 - 0.2*2 = 2.0 - 0.6 - 0.4 - 0.4 = 0.6 -> put in Customer/Emergent lane or schedule for next cycle depending on capacity.
decision_matrix: Tradeoff priority order when capacity short: 1) Keep Core Roadmap items that are on-path for customer SLAs or contractual commitments. 2) Defer lowest-scored Core items first. 3) If emergent high-impact customer work arrives (score >=3) swap with the lowest-scoring Core item after leader sign-off. 4) Experiments are pre-emptible except where running to statistical power requires completion (product confirms).
escalation_triggers: Automatic escalation to PM+ENG+TPM when: 1) projected slippage of Core Roadmap > 10% of committed scope, 2) incident creates >3 person-days unplanned work in a single week, or 3) a sales-backed customer request with potential ARR >= $50k appears. Escalation path: PM -> Eng Lead -> VP Product for final decision within 48 hours.
communication_playbook: When a scope cut or swap is executed: 1) Publish update to #cycle-status channel with: affected tickets, rationale (scoring & landing zone), owner for follow-up, and remediation plan. 2) Send short note to impacted customers (if any) within 24h. 3) Create a retro ticket to capture lessons and update the playbook if pattern repeats more than twice in a quarter.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page Confluence playbook exists with the rules above and a sample filled landing zone for an example team.
PM/Eng/Design leads have signed off on the lane definitions and the scoring rubric.
A simple spreadsheet or dashboard (team-level) can be used to calculate scores and show live capacity allocation.
A comms template for cuts/swaps and an example email are published in the playbook.
rollout_plan: 1) Draft playbook and run a dry-run with two volunteer teams during this cycle. 2) Collect feedback and iterate (one week). 3) Publish final playbook in Confluence and add a short training session in next all-hands or PM sync. 4) Add automated scoring column to our Cycle Dashboard (owner: Eng Data).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly rigid allocations lead to underutilization; Mitigation: review lanes at mid-cycle checkpoint and allow +/-10% rebalancing.
Risk: Scoring becomes politicized; Mitigation: require evidence (metrics links) for Impact scores and require two approvers for swaps.
Risk: Teams game the buffer; Mitigation: include historical burn-rate as a hidden tie-breaker in the dashboard.
decisions: Adopt 60/15/15/10 default lane split for cross-functional teams; teams <6 headcount may compress lanes to 70/20/10.
Require written PM+Eng lead sign-off for any swap that touches Core Roadmap.
Automate a 'score' column in the Cycle Dashboard and surface top 5 emergent requests weekly.
